title: Perf run 20261018-0317
heading: A phone shows the start page's board sooner, first visit and returning: leaned on the landed code, one named trade-off on the desktop's first click
meta:
This run keeps two changes to the start page's picture of the board (SWR, SP3) and one fix to how the bench times it (PB1). SWR was called better by its own A/B: a returning phone's board 576 → 356 ms. SP3, a phone's own cut of the picture, was called better alone on a draft tree (796 → 564 ms); on the landed code it leaned the phone's board 920 → 612 ms (−28%, 11 of 12 pairs) and cut the phone's bytes by a third, not called. It also leaned the desktop's first click 6.5 ms slower (11 of 12 pairs). A settle step parked SP3 for that; the orchestrator kept it as a named trade-off the owner can veto (see Needs from me).

The final A/B ran on 8e26575 (SWR and SP3, the app as it is now) against the base db54330, over 11 interleaved pairs: the returning phone's board 620 → 340 ms (−44%, 11 of 11 pairs faster), not called. All 16 headline rows were measured there, and none was called better or worse.

The PR also carries the loop state: the ledger, the scoreboard and this run's record. Origin/main (2be67f6, 8bcb6a1) was merged in before the final checks.

needs.intro: One trade-off for you to accept or veto (SP3). The other two items are information, each with a recommendation.

items.title: Trade-off: SP3 buys a phone's board ~300 ms sooner with a desktop first click 6.5 ms slower (yours to veto)
items.body:
CLAUDE.md asks for a change that buys one player moment with another to be named, so here it is. SP3 was measured on the landed code: f0431f6 against f0431f6 with SP3 reverted (e2a2e03), cold load, 12 pairs (ab-20261018-0317-sp3-landed.md). Nothing was called. Median pair, head ÷ base:

  • Gain: phone board 920 → 612 ms, −28% geomean, ×0.665, 11 of 12 better. One pair at 2.43 blocks the call. Phone bytes 417 → 235 KiB (−33%).
  • Cost: desktop first click 13.3 → 19.8 ms, +6.5 ms, ×1.41, 11 of 12 worse, not called. The likely cause: the head's preload script grew from 439 to 2,564 bytes on every page, desktop included.
  • Desktop board ×1.20, 8 of 12 worse; identical code gave ×1.233 in an A/A, so this row is noise.

The look was clean: each tree built and shown at 360x740, 390x844, 430x932, 844x390 and 1280x800, first paint, handover and live preview. Upright phones see the same framing and sharpness; the handover has no jump or ghosting; landscape and desktop are pixel-identical.

A settle step parked SP3 for the click's lean. The orchestrator kept it (5cdc50c): you accepted a trade of this kind and larger on 2026-10-17 (a returning phone's page 144 ms sooner for a first click 17 ms slower, "okay with this trade if it's not too slow and if users are unlikely to notice it"). No one perceives 6.5 ms on a click; a phone's board ~300 ms sooner and a third fewer bytes is visible on a mobile network.
items.recommend: Keep SP3. To veto it, revert 5cdc50c. Either way, the ledger's FC1 wins the click back: run the phone-tall choice in the head only where it can apply.

items.title: The 1.2× target was not met (information)
items.body: Over all 16 headline rows the branch is ×1.104 as fast as the base (ab-20261018-0317-final.md). The rows for a phone's start page moved most: board ×0.69 at the median pair, returning board ×0.59, usable −7.4%. The other rows' code did not change, so they were not expected to move. Meeting the target needs wins on the computer's, joining's and review's rows. This run's focus was the start page. The one idea for the computer's row (RT1) leaned 17% faster but was not called.
items.recommend: Retry RT1 with 16 or more pairs in the next speed run.

items.title: Four rows leaned slower on the final commit, none called (information)
items.body:
The speed rule lists every headline row more than 3% worse at its median pair. In the final A/B (11 pairs, head ÷ base):

  • Desktop usable ×1.096, 7 of 11 worse: 1.52 0.65 1.43 0.61 0.89 1.19 1.06 1.10 1.22 0.29 4.43.
  • Desktop board ×1.043, 6 of 11: 1.95 1.10 0.96 0.31 0.56 0.82 1.06 1.04 2.94 1.39 0.53.
  • Desktop first click ×1.055, 7 of 11: 2.06 1.16 1.06 0.93 0.99 1.03 1.80 0.73 1.23 0.70 8.19.
  • Search speed ×1.035, 6 of 11: 1.03 1.50 1.66 0.20 1.32 0.99 0.98 0.88 1.43 0.37 2.67. The branch changes no search code.

Identical code compared with itself leaned as far: the A/A at the start of the run gave desktop usable ×1.033 (3 of 3) and desktop board ×1.233 (3 of 3). The final commit has SWR and SP3, as the branch does now. The first chart shows the final pairs; the next two show the same desktop rows in the two A/As on identical code. Earlier in the run the desktop board leaned ×1.251 with SP3 alone (9 of 12 worse). On a desktop, SP3 changes only the small script in the page's head that starts the picture's download (439 → 2,564 bytes). No mechanism for a slower desktop has been found. On the landed code the desktop board leaned ×1.20 with SP3 (8 of 12) and the first click ×1.41 (11 of 12): the trade-off above.
items.recommend: Keep SWR and SP3. The ledger's DL1 measures the desktop rows' A/A spread (board, usable, first click) with 16 pairs; FC1 wins back the first click.

changed.intro: Two changes to the start page and one fix to the bench. SWR was called better in its own A/B, SP3 in its own on a draft tree; on the final commit both rows leaned faster but were not called (Scoreboard). SP3 is kept as a named trade-off (Needs from me).

items.title: A returning phone shows the board sooner (SWR, 7799513)
items.body: The start page's pictures are now asked for with a version in the address (?v= and a hash of the pictures), and the host keeps them for a year. A returning phone takes the picture from its cache without first asking the server whether it changed. Re-rendered pictures get a new hash, so a new address. Alone: returning phone board 576 → 356 ms, called better, every pair 0.52–0.75; requests 2 → 1. On the final app: 620 → 340 ms, every pair better (0.39–0.71), not called.

items.title: A phone shows the start page's board sooner (SP3, 14cdae3; parked in ecfd0bc, restored in 5cdc50c)
items.body: Upright phones get a cut of the phone picture shaped like their screen (phone-tall): 2.2 million pixels instead of 6.8 million, same lens and composition, on the windows it covers (360x740 to 430x932). The head's preload, the early picture and LandingPicture share one choice, and the picture shown stays while it still covers the window, so a phone's browser bars never fetch the other one. Alone on a draft tree: phone board 796 → 564 ms, called better, 12 of 12. On the landed code: 920 → 612 ms, −28%, 11 of 12, not called; phone bytes 417 → 235 KiB. Cost: the desktop's first click +6.5 ms (Needs from me).

items.title: The bench times the picture when the browser paints it (PB1, bcaa032)
items.body: The board rows now use the browser's own paint time for the picture (Element Timing) instead of a script's view of it, which waited on the page's main thread. Both sides of every later A/B measure this way. An A/A showed its spread is no worse than the old stamp's.

items.title: Each new check fails when its code is broken
items.body: Verify broke each kept change on purpose and ran its tests. Seven breaks, all caught: the version left out of the inline scripts, the year rule missing, the version ignoring the files' contents, and, for SP3, the shown picture not kept, coverage always true, and two ways for the head's download to disagree with the page. With the paint timing broken, the bench's count of untimed pictures read 2 of 2 loads.

  • The ledger rows for SWR, SP3 and PB1 (kept). SP3's cost on the desktop's first click is the new open row FC1.
  • The computer section's raw way-in steps (7dcca62, 10 lines of the bench): they fed no row and served only RT1, which is parked. They wait as bench/loop/patches/way-in-steps-RT1.patch.
  • 229f71a's rewrap of two ARCHITECTURE.md paragraphs (no words changed), reverted.

rejected.intro: One idea was tried and parked with its patch.

items.title: RT1: render an already-loaded chunk at once
items.body: React holds back revealing a lazily loaded part until 300 ms after its placeholder first showed, even when the part's code is already loaded. On every base load, the computer's game screen arrived about 300 ms after its address. RT1 renders a loaded chunk directly. Against its parent, 12 pairs on the computer's section: the first board picture 1.37 → 1.14 s, ×0.83 at the median pair, 10 of 12 pairs better. Not called, because two pairs went the other way. Parked as patches/lazy-chunk-no-throttle-RT1.patch, with a test that fails on the base.

choices.intro:
• Did not bisect the computer's lean (CL1). The new way-in steps showed React's 300 ms hold on every base load, a likelier cause than any one commit, and the time went to RT1.
  • Measured SP3 alone on a draft tree, as asked, then merged it onto SWR. The scoreboard rows for that A/B are labelled with that tree.
  • Kept SP3 at first, though its row was not called on the tree as landed. After grading, SP3 was measured on the landed code and parked by the keep rule for the desktop first click's lean; the orchestrator then overrode that and kept it as a named trade-off, of the kind and size the owner accepted on 2026-10-17 (Needs from me).
  • Ran step 2 as a short A/A, because the base's app code is the last base's byte for byte.
  • Merged origin/main before the final checks. In the CLAUDE.md conflict, kept this branch's landing-pictures line and main's readme-image line.
  • Rendered the final A/B from its 11 complete pairs after the 2-hour limit stopped pair 12. Then stopped a cold-load-only 12-pair re-check after one pair: the machine had slowed to about 8 minutes a side, so it needed about 3.3 hours.
  • Did not rewrite the kept commits' messages. Their percentages are from their own A/Bs; this page and the PR say what holds on the final commit.
  • After the grade, tried once more for a called result on the phone's board rows: a 10-pair cold-load re-check of the final tree. The machine slowed until most sides timed out, and the 2-hour limit stopped it in pair 9; only two pairs were whole, so no report was kept. Worded the headline as leaned, not called.
  • Dropped the raw way-in steps (7dcca62) and kept them as a patch beside RT1's.

notConfirmed.intro:
• Why the desktop board and first click lean slower with SP3: no trace was taken (ledger DL1, FC1).
  • RT1's 300 ms hold: read from raw output that is not committed, from a bench patch now parked with RT1 (ledger BR1 would put the steps in the reports).
  • A called result for the returning phone's board on the final app: it leaned faster in 11 of 11 pairs but was not called.
  • How the picture's cache rule behaves on the real host: the bench serves the built _headers through vite preview over HTTP/1.1.
